newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Shenzhen B shares inch lower in slow trade.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen B shares inch lower in slow trade.

text.p: Shenzhen's B share index closed slightly lower on Thursday with most institutions adopting a wait-and-see attitude towards trading ahead of the corporate report season, brokers said.
The B share index shed 0.79 points or 0.56 percent to end at 141.65 on volume of 6.49 million shares worth HK$31.70 million against Wednesday's HK$27.56 million.

The A share index edged up 0.98 points or 0.29 percent to close at 342.86 on turnover of 3.06 billion yuan compared with 3.56 billion yuan in the previous session, due in part to speculative buying, brokers said.
An increasing number of investors in the A and B stock markets have moved onto the sidelines ahead of the corporate reporting season, which will start in March, they said.
The Shenzhen Stock Exchange will be closed between February 3 and February 16 for the Chinese lunar new year holiday with trading resuming on February 17.
"Few institutions are willing to engage in large-scale trading before the long holiday," a broker said.
Guangdong Expressway was the worst B share performer, falling HK$0.20 or 2.77 percent to HK$7.02 on thin trade of 46,200 shares.

Shenzhen Petrochemical followed with a decline of HK$0.09 or 2.77 percent to HK$3.90 on volume of only 6,500 shares. Southern Glass traded the most on volume of 822,600 shares and slipped HK$0.10 to HK$4.39.
Television maker Shenzhen Huafa bucked the trend with a rise of HK$0.06 or 1.69 percent to HK$3.62 as 29,800 shares changed hands, making it the session's strongest performer.

On the A share market, refrigerator maker Changsha Zhongyi, which has a venture with Swedish firm Electrolux, climbed 0.35 yuan or 5.95 percent to 6.23 yuan on the day's heaviest trade of 19.58 million shares due to speculative buying by institutions, brokers said.
